analysis.title: JPM US Market Intelligence - Afternoon Briefing (November 17, 2026)
key_insights: US stocks closed lower on Nov 17: SPX -1.0%, NDX -0.7%, RTY -1.5%. Breadth was weak, with RSP -1.4% vs SPY -1.0%. Mag 7 fell 0.7% and modestly outperformed SPX (MSFT -2.3%, GOOG -1.3%, META -1.2%, NVDA -0.5%).

Software fell 3.3% ahead of NVDA earnings while semis rose 0.3%. The JPM desk cites mixed or negative Cleveland checks for WDAY and CRM, and a JPM preview from S. Chatterjee saying AI monetization is slower despite real adoption.

After the close NVDA reported Q3 earnings and Q4 guidance and the stock rose 4%. Per JPM trader Brian Heavey, Q4 revenue guidance is $130B vs a survey of $129B, and gross margin guidance is 71-72% vs JPM's 72%.

NVDA's CFO said Hopper shipments to China in Q3 were $2.4B. The company still includes no China revenue in its outlook. The desk is watching the 5PM call for comment on the 70% FY27/F28 sales growth figure.

JPM US Market Intel calls the October retail sales print strong, including prior-month revisions. Consumption of $748.2B sets a record, and post-COVID retail sales growth is roughly double the 2014-2019 rate.

JPM argues SPX EPS is tied more to nominal GDP than real GDP, so higher inflation is not a problem for earnings. It adds that the strong consumer and tight labor markets may add hawkishness from the Fed. Inflation is called the biggest risk for 27Q1.

Fedspeak leaned hawkish. Musalem warned four more hikes could be needed by spring, Williams said no dramatic action is needed, and Hammack supports small, steady hikes. Treasuries rallied, led by the front end (2y -2bp, 10y -2.2bp).

JPM US Market Intel is tactically bullish and likes owning stocks into year-end. It sees positioning as cleaner and entry points as more attractive, and thinks a 50bp Fed hike in December is highly unlikely.

Monetization Menu (Nov 16): the anti-AI and ex-Tech rotation has dominated 26H2. JPM favors moving back to Tech, with primary exposure to Mag7 and options to play an AI rebound. Within ex-Tech it prefers Cyclicals over Defensives, and it likes Europe for Cyclical/Value exposure.

Earlier Monetization Menu (Nov 11): the tech washout appears at or near completion, with some risk of another semis decline. JPM would consider US memory and semis via options and sees more upside in European cyclicals than US ones.

In Europe, markets closed lower (SX5E -2.1%, DAX -2.1%, UKX -1.8%). European semis fell 2.8% on US China AI-chip and data-center curbs, and DBK fell 6.0%. UK unemployment was 4.6% vs 4.7% survey, and German ZEW was 35.6 vs 28.8 survey.

Desk comments on HD: the quarter was solid with the best comp since the COVID period. Guidance took sales to the high end of the prior range, margin to the lower end and EPS growth to the midpoint, which blessed the Street's +1.6% SSS and $2.81 4Q EPS. Briggs Barton expects a muted stock reaction given the run into the print.

On NKE, the desk says investors are skeptical of the $3.00-3.50 long-term EPS guide, which is at least 30% ahead of expectations while the stock is only up 2%. Bears think management has set a high bar that leads to disappointment and negative revisions.

market_movers.rationale: Q3 results and Q4 guidance of $130B revenue vs a $129B survey, and the stock rose 4% after hours. The company excludes China revenue from its outlook.
JPM's Chris Horvers calls the print solid with the best comp since the COVID boom. He expects a muted stock reaction given the run into the print.
The stock faded its initial gain after the investor day. Investors doubt the $3.00-3.50 long-term EPS guide, and bears expect negative revisions.
DBK fell 6.0%, the main single-stock drag in Europe. The note gives no reason.

JPM prefers Cyclicals over Defensives as the growth narrative restarts and the Fed turns more hawkish.
JPM cites relative positioning and valuation, and notes that another surge in the USD could temper outperformance.
The desk reports broad-based selling in software (enterprise apps, security, infrastructure) with mixed or negative checks, and gives no formal view.

earnings_insights: NVDA Q3 reported after the close on 11/17. Q4 revenue guidance is $130B vs survey $129B. Gross margin guidance is 71-72% vs JPM's 72%. Q3 Hopper shipments to China were $2.4B, with no China revenue in the outlook. The stock rose 4% after hours.

HD Q3 reported 11/17. Guidance took sales to the high end of the prior range, margin to the lower end and EPS growth to the midpoint. This essentially blessed the Street's 4Q SSS of +1.6% and EPS of $2.81 (Street estimates). September was the best month, October was positive, and DIY was up in 3Q with Pro still leading.
NKE investor day on 11/17 gave a long-term EPS guide of $3.00-3.50, per the desk at least 30% ahead of expectations. The stock was up only 2%.
Earnings due 11/18: LOW, P, PANW, TGT, TJX, WWD. Due 11/19: INTU, KEYS, ROAD, ROST, WMT, WSM. Due 11/20: BMNR, CPRT, IESC, VEEV.

geopolitical: Washington's China AI-chip and data-center curbs weighed on European semis, which fell 2.8%.
The US banned China optical receivers (FCC), which lifted optical names pre-market, but the gains barely held.
A US Democratic senator introduced a bill to end China's trade status ahead of the Trump-Xi meeting.
The US and China agreed to extend the trade truce through January 20, 2027.
The APEC Economic Leaders Meeting is in Shenzhen on Nov 18-19.
